properties.decision:
@ajs, 2026-10-05: "we had brainstormed about creating a sligara7.github.io/reflow2 page (now would flo2-connector.github.io/reflow2 I'd imagine) ... I think the new github.io page should have the instructions as you laid them out. It should have the basic setup (which is what we use here); it should have the setup instructions for how I use it at work; and it should have the instructions for how Alex uses it at his work. I think that is the minimum we can start with for our page. We can add to it later, but that's how I'd like to start. I like the black background and white text and green buttons like we used on flo2.io." He also asked that the names and details specific to any one person or workplace be removed.

Asked whether that reopens dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page (accepted 2026-08-14, reaffirmed 2026-09-28: the public page carries ONLY renderings generated from reflow2's own design), he chose, the same day: "Setup hand-written (Recommended)".

THEN, THE SAME EVENING, he asked for an explainer too: "yes, it was the untracked docs/project-brain.html; that was my project brain for my work, but if we can make that more generic (make up some fictional, but simple to understand project brain), that would be great ... I do think the generic version of untracked docs/project-brain.html could be used in the flo2-connector.github.io pages to explain what it is." Asked how that fits the rule, he chose: "Allow explainer pages (Recommended)".

WHAT IS SETTLED:
- Pages addressed to someone who does not have reflow2 yet are written by hand: SETUP pages, and EXPLAINER pages that say what reflow2 is through a clearly made-up example. COORD.md's rule puts that kind of text in a document ("a document holds what is addressed to someone without the tool; the graph holds what the tool can compute").
- Any page that shows a REAL design's content (its counts, views, reports or status) stays generated from that design, as the 2026-08-14 decision requires. So the explainer carries no real number: the owner's one-pager showed reflow2's own counts and a growth chart from its git history, and those are left out rather than copied by hand.
- The first pages: index.html, the explainer, drawn after the owner's Project Brain one-pager and re-told through a made-up school robotics team (the Gearheads); and setup.html, three setup paths (your own computer with an MCP agent; VS Code where an organisation blocks third-party MCP; a server for a team from the container image). No real person or workplace is named.
- Laid out like flo2.io, in its dark palette: black background, light text, green buttons.
- The address is flo2-connector.github.io/reflow2, since the repository moved to the flo2-connector organisation on 2026-10-03.

CHOSEN BY THE IMPLEMENTER, AS THE DEFAULT THE REQUIREMENT ITSELF POINTED TO (the owner can override): Pages is published by an Actions deploy of site/ (.github/workflows/pages.yml), not from the root, /docs or a gh-pages branch, because the root is a Rust workspace. Version numbers and image digests are left off the setup page and linked to the latest release instead, so the page is not wrong after the next cut.

NOT IN THIS STEP, AND STILL INTENT under req:reflow2-has-a-public-page-anyone-can-read: the minimal README, and moving the documentation out of docs/ into generated pages. The repository clean-up the owner mentioned is not part of this step either.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-05 — reflow2's site is written by hand where it addresses someone without reflow2: an explainer told through a made-up example, and three setup paths. Any page that shows a REAL design's content stays generated from that design
properties.rationale: Setup steps and an explainer are what a newcomer needs first, and they are the one kind of page the repository's own rule says belongs in a document rather than in the design. Generating them from the graph would mean writing install commands and a made-up team into a design only to render them back out. The carve-out is kept to pages that make no claim to come from a real design, so the reason for the 2026-08-14 decision (a page claiming 'this came from the graph' is falsified by one hand-written fact) still holds for every page that shows a design.
